text:
maria: quick sync - followup on autoscale approach. i'm worried a fully central scheduler will be a chokepoint + make dedicated pools brittle. thoughts?

alex: agree. central visibility is valuable but admission should live with the pool. keep decision local, allow advisory signals.

saurabh: local admission + advisory hints is my +1. but we need a clear contract so operators can apply consistent fallback rules.

jess: proposal: two-part surface: 1) /admit(request) sync RPC, very small. 2) a pubsub of hints (score, ttl, variant_pref). hints are advisory only.

lina: what does /admit return exactly? minimal fields plz so it's cheap to call.

maria: minimal: {accepted:bool, wait_for_ms:int, ticket_id:str, variant:str, eta_s:int}. keep names short.

alex: add a "reason" string for observability (e.g., "no-headroom", "rate-limit", "ok-warm"). helps SRE debugging.

saurabh: prewarm credits: we should budget prewarms per-tenant. token-bucket per-tenant. starting a warm consumes N tokens. quick shutdowns refund fraction.
jess: refund schedule suggestion (different from earlier RFC): <5s -> 90% refund, 5-30s -> 60%, 30-120s -> 25%, >120s -> 0. keeps incentives to stay up.
lina: how do we surface token usage? metrics: tokens_consumed_total, tokens_refunded_total, active_tickets. traces for ticket lifecycle.
maria: also emit events when hints are applied: hint_seen, hint_applied, hint_ignored (with reason). need to debug divergence between central score and local load.
alex: hysteresis: require both score > threshold and sustained local CPU/RAM/KV-cache utilization for X secs before prewarm. prevents flash prewarms.
saurabh: implement smoothing window on central score (e.g., EMA with alpha = 0.2) so transient spikes don't force churn.
jess: rollout strategy: start with hints disabled on all operators. enable hints for a single team/pool, monitor metrics for 48h, then grad expand. default is local-only.
lina: security: hints signed and versioned. operator validates TTL and signature. central cannot force variant changes; only recommend.
maria: API example (tiny):

```json
{
  "request_id": "r_123",
  "tenant": "acme",
  "slo_ms": 200,
  "cost_tier": "low"
}
// response
{
  "accepted": true,
  "wait_for_ms": 0,
  "ticket_id": "tk_789",
  "variant": "gpt-q4x_lowmem",
  "eta_s": 0,
  "reason": "ok-warm"
}
```

alex: note: ticket_id lifecycle is important. operator should expose ticket_state transitions: issued -> warm-started -> idle -> terminated -> refunded. logs help reimburse tokens.
saurabh: rate limit /admit to protect operator control plane. also cap variant flips to 1 per minute per-tenant to avoid model churn.
jess: validation tests: unit tests for refund logic, integration test that simulates two pools racing for the same tenant hints, chaos test for hint consumer dropping messages.
lina: ops-bot: please create a dashboard with: prewarm_fail_rate, ticket_refunds_per_min, avg_admit_latency, hint_apply_ratio.
ops-bot: created dashboard "prewarm-credit-health" and added owners @eng-runtime-sre, link: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd1234/prewarm-credit-health
maria: for docs i'll open an RFC follow-up with the contract, refund table, metrics, and rollout checklist. linking it to the original autoscale rfc.
alex: sounds good. i'd like a follow-up item: simulation of tenant-level token economics (how many tokens to allocate per plan).
saurabh: i'll draft a simulator notebook and share. aim to avoid starvation for high-SLA tenants.
jess: ok dev plan: 1) admissions shim + /admit impl, 2) hint consumer + opt-in flag, 3) metrics/events + tests, 4) canary rollout. PRs after design doc.
maria: thanks all. i'll capture action items in the RFC issue.
